Condition of railway yards and
washing lines
†*141. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that the condition of the railway
yards and washing lines located in Delhi
has so much deteriorated that any serious
mishap may occur there at any time;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
employees working there have been
demanding for repairs for the last five years;
(c) if so, the action taken, so far, by
Government for improvement in the
condition; and
(d) by when, reconstruction work of
the buildings of the railway yards and
washing lines would be completed?
Approval of dangerous projects and
industries
†*142. SHRIMATI KUM KUM
RAI: Will the Minister of
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that during the
last two years Government have given
clearance to such type of projects and
industries which are very dangerous from
environmental point of view; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Clinical trials by multinational
companies
*143. SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) what is Government's policy
regarding clinical trials being conducted by
multinational companies in the country;
(b) the steps taken by Government for
regulating such clinical trials;
(c) whether Government have any
mechanism to monitor/regulate such
medical trials;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Introduction of trains running 100
Km. per hour
*144. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have any
proposal to introduce trains in Andhra
Pradesh which run at 100 Km. per hour;
(b) if so, whether Government have
identified any routes for this purpose;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether Government have
conducted any trial before introducing these
trains;
(e) if so, the details thereof;
(f) the time-frame set to introduce these
trains; and
(g) the details of extra expenditure likely
to be incurred for this purpose?
Ban on smoking scenes in films and
TV serials
*145. SHRI LALIT SURI: Will the
Minister of  HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have imposed
a ban on smoking scenes in films and
Television serials with effect from
2nd October, 2005;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the reaction of film industry, if any,
received by Government; and
(d) how Government propose to tackle
foreign films having smoking scenes released
in theatres?
Crops under NCIS
*146. DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) the names and details of the crops
which are presently covered under the
National Crop Insurance Scheme;
(b) the names and details of those new
crops which are presently under
consideration for being covered under the
scheme;
(c) whether the scheme is being
implemented in the whole country;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) if not, the reasons therefor;
(f) the total number of farmers in the
country, and out of them, the total number
of farmers who have got the benefits of the
scheme during the last three years,
year-wise and State-wise;
(g) whether any target was fixed for the
coverage under the Scheme during
2005-2006; and
(h) if so, the target achieved upto date?
Funds for agricultural research
*147.SHRI S. ANBALAGAN: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) the funds allocated during each of
the last three years for agricultural research,
State-wise;
(b) the achievements made in regard to
higher productivity in the field of agriculture
as a result of these researches;
(c) whether any high-yielding varieties
of paddy and wheat were produced during
these years;
(d) if so, the details thereof and the steps
taken/being taken to popularize the same
among the farmers;
(e) whether it is a fact that per-hectare
productivity of wheat and paddy is very
low when compared to other countries

47
particularly the western countries and the
far east; and
(f) if so, the reasons therefor and the
steps proposed to be taken thereon?
Allowing imported deep sea fishing
vessels in EEZ
*148. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are
implementing a policy to allow imported
deep sea fishing vessels on deferred
payments to fish in our EEZ;
(b) if so, the number of such trawlers
which fished in 2003-04 and 2004-05;
(c) whether Government are aware that
new conditions and new restrictions make
it impossible for such ventures to succeed
and the spirit of the original policy is being
vitiated;
(d) the objectives of such activities; and
(e) the steps proposed to adopt a pro-
active role?
Making KVK system contemporary
*149. SHRIMATI S. G. INDIRA:  Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are considering to make Krishi Vigyan
Kendra system contemporary;
(b) if so, the steps taken in this regard;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
Government had set up Agriculture
Technology Management Agencies in
several districts; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Indebtedness of farmers in Andhra
Pradesh
*150. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY:
SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO:
 Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that according to
the latest Sample Survey Organisation's
Report, 82 per cent of the farm holdings in
Andhra Pradesh are suffering from
indebtedness;
(b) whether it is also a fact that in spite
of high GDP growth and agricultural
prosperity, nearly half of the farm holdings
in the country are indebted at various
degrees; and
(c) if so, the action Government are
taking to reduce indebtedness in the
country, with particular reference to Andhra
Pradesh?
Growth of FPIs
†*151. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
 Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the annual
growth rate of food processing industries
in the country remained at around 6 per
cent in the past;
(b) if not, the annual growth rate
assessed from the period 2000 to 2004;
(c) whether it is also a fact that there are
ample opportunities for growth of the said
industry in the country; and
(d) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

48
Fixing profit margin on drugs
†*152. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI  RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS  be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that no maximum
limit for earning share of profit by the drug
manufacturers in the drug manufacturing
industry has been fixed in the present price
fixation policy;
(b) if so, the facts in this regard and the
percentage of the share of profit being
earned by drug manufacturers at present in
comparison to the average manufacturing
cost;
(c) whether it is also a fact that a
committee under the chairmanship of a
Joint Secretary has been constituted by
Government to decide the limit of trade-
margin in the drug industry; and
(d) if so, the facts in this regard and by
when the said committee would submit its
final report?
Unauthorised homoeopathic medical
colleges in Assam
*153.SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMUR: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that some
unregistered private homoeopathic colleges
are mushrooming without affiliation from
either the Central Council of Homoeopathy
or the Assam State Homoeopathic Board,
which affects the reputation of the
homoeopathic system of medicine and also
exposes the patients seeking treatment to a
grave danger;
(b) whether Government have taken any
measures to identify such bogus
institutions; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Rise in prices of essential
commodities
*154.SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the hardships being faced by the public at
large on account of abnormal rise in the
prices of essential commodities in general
and specially of onion and other vegetables
during the months of October and
November, 2005;
(b) if so, the specific reasons for the
steep rise in prices of all the commodities
which had hurt the lower strata of the
Society; and
(c) the remedial steps proposed to be
taken in this regard?
MSP for Rajasthan crops
†*155. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE  be pleased to state
whether there is any scheme to buy main
crops from Rajasthan such as gwar,
corriander, cumin, isabgoal, onion and garlic
at support price?
Decline in growth rate of foodgrain
production
*156.SHRIMATI SUKHBUNS
KAUR: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that annual growth
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

49
rate of foodgrain production has slipped
from 16 per cent in 1991-96 to merely 2.9
per cent in 2001-05;
(b) if so, the reasons for such a fall; and
(c) the special steps contemplated for
the last phase of the Tenth Five Year Plan
to improve this growth rate and the targets
fixed for these years?
Model stations in Uttar Pradesh
†*157. PROF. M. M. AGARWAL: Will
the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have
formulated any plan to give model look to
some of the stations in the State of Uttar
Pradesh under the Tenth Five Year Plan;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the amount allocated for this purpose
and the number of stations made as model
stations, so far; and
(d) the amount spent thereon, so far?
Cotton variety by CICR
*158. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Central
Institute for Cotton Research (CICR) has
been able to introduce the Cryl Ac gene in
an Indian cotton variety and the Institute's
Bt variety is likely to hit the market in the
next two years; and
(b) if so, the special features of the
CICR's Bt variety?
Scheme for health infrastructure
development in rural areas
†*159. SHRI BASHISTHA
NARAIN SINGH: Will the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of Government schemes
to develop infrastructure relating to health
in rural areas;
(b) the funds reserved for rural areas
under Health for All Scheme;
(c) whether any special scheme would
be formulated to provide medical facilities
at a cheaper rate in view of economic
condition of rural poor; and
(d) if so, the expected outline thereof?
Supreme Court directive on drug
price control
*160. SHRI MANOJ
BHATTACHARYA: Will the Minister of
CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Hon'ble Supreme Court
of India had directed the Government in
2003 to formulate appropriate criteria to
ensure that essential and life saving drugs
do not fall outside the ambit of price
control;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
Government had promised to make all life
saving drugs available at reasonable prices
and if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the details of the steps taken, so far,
to honour the Supreme Court's directive
and the commitment made in by
Government?
NEW DELHI; YOGENDRA NARAIN,
The 26th November, 2005 Secretary-General.
